content: The medication is administered intravenously at a dosage of 6 mg/kg, given at intervals of 1 to 5 days, for a total of 9 to 10 doses. Potential adverse effects include hypertension, myocardial damage, encephalopathy, peripheral neuropathy, colic, vomiting, albuminuria, and a Herxheimer-type reaction. It is contraindicated in individuals with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency or hypersensitivity to the drug. Regarding pregnancy, no studies have been conducted to assess its safety, and it is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk during lactation. However, in general, drugs classified under Pregnancy Category A are considered safe, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. The drug works by inhibiting the synthesis of ATP, which is essential for the survival of the parasite. It has a volume of distribution (Vd) of 100 L/kg, crosses the blood-brain barrier, and has a mean terminal elimination half-life of 35 hours. The drug is primarily excreted through urine.
